Yes: the supplied papers suggest two practical ways to inspect activations during inference with low slowdown. For model-serving observability, DMI-Lib decouples internal-state collection from the inference hot path using an asynchronous observability substrate, preserving serving optimizations and tight GPU memory budgets; it reports only modest overhead in offline and online serving and lowers latency overhead versus similar baselines [7]. For multi-GPU interpretability, another system scales activation-level inspection to large models while reducing activation memory and increasing throughput, sustaining collection of full layer-wise activation trajectories during generation [4].

If you want inspection for decision-making rather than raw tracing, lightweight readers of internal states can also avoid much extra cost. Gnosis passively observes hidden states and attention patterns, compresses them into fixed-budget descriptors, and predicts correctness with negligible inference cost [1]. Related work also uses internal activations for early correctness prediction and early stopping, reducing token usage by pruning weak trajectories early [9].
